title: The Last Blade
subtitle: Blades at the end of an era
summary: The Last Blade is SNK's weapon-based fighting game, first released for Neo Geo MVS in Japan on 5 December 1997.
body: The Last Blade is SNK's weapon-based fighting game, first released for Neo Geo MVS in Japan on 5 December 1997. Its cast fights during the Bakumatsu period, drawing the setting's tensions together with supernatural imagery and Japanese mythology. Carefully staged backgrounds and restrained passages of music give the encounters a distinctive atmosphere. Before fighting, the player chooses between Power and Speed styles. That decision changes how the character can build attacks, placing a strategic preference alongside the choice of fighter before the first exchange has even begun.

Power mode increases damage and provides access to particularly strong techniques under the necessary conditions. Speed mode allows normal attacks to link into longer sequences and special moves. The same character therefore supports different priorities: a player may seek a decisive opening or prefer to keep an opponent inside a connected series of strikes. Learning the chosen style means understanding both its opportunities and the situations in which it is vulnerable. The selection makes a return to a familiar fighter another chance to approach the round differently.

A dedicated deflection command lets the player answer an incoming attack and leave the opponent briefly open. Its timing gives defence a precise, active role within the weapon exchanges. The period setting also shapes the sound, with music drawing on orchestral textures suited to the nineteenth-century atmosphere. Hiroshi Yamazoe, Yasuhiro Naka and Yasuo Yamate contributed to the score. The Last Blade connects these measured surroundings to a combat system built around a small number of consequential choices: style, distance, commitment and the instant at which a strike can be turned aside.
